Subject: Re: Eval runbook question: acceptance path + exception handling

Jordan —

High level from PM/QA side: here is a minimal acceptance checklist we can push to Acme for the pilot sign-off. I kept it short so procurement doesn't stall.

- Functional correctness: top-3 intents for the promptset >= 90% precision on a stratified 500 sample.
- Safety floor: zero critical PII leakage incidents on 5k sampled requests; no critical policy violations.
- Regression delta: automated evaluation metric (BLEU-like + embedding sim) shows <= 3% drop vs baseline on the same sample.
- Latency: 95th percentile generation <= 600ms for the expected token distribution.
- Usability sanity: subjective rating from Acme SME >= 4/5 on 30 hand-evals.

Exception handling (proposal):
- Alerting: quality-delta > threshold triggers triage channel (#eval-triage) and pages the on-call ML infra lead.
- Immediate action: switch routing to the last-known-good model variant (pinned model) while we diagnose.
- Owner flow: PM (Jordan) coordinates with ML infra (Karthik) for rollback; Marissa leads QA verification.
- Escalation: if rollback not possible within 30m, CS/Eng leadership gets looped for customer communication.

I'll add these to the runbook and tag SUP-4247.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Lead, Evaluation & Quality, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2028-03-22T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval runbook question: acceptance path + exception handling

Adding a few technical constraints / acceptance specifics from infra/runtime:

- Canary config: start at 5% traffic for Acme for the AB, move to 25% after 24h if metrics are green, then 100% after 72h. Any regression at 25% or 72h checkpoints triggers a mandatory freeze.
- Rollback options: we can 1) route to pinned float32 model, 2) route to a lower-capacity quantized variant with guaranteed correctness tests, or 3) apply a prompt-layer safety shim (prefix filter) as an emergency mitigation.
- Notification automation: SUP-4247 should include a webhook to create a Jira incident (SUP-4247-INC) when the evaluation pipeline posts a regression score above threshold. That incident must include the sample failing prompts and the KV-cache hit rates.
- Acceptance automation: we will supply a reproducible evaluation notebook and the seed sample used for the 500-stratified checks (attached promptset_v4.jsonl).

I'll drop a small appendix in the runbook describing the rollback latency expectations (we can route within ~90s for routing changes; full model redeploy ~15-20m).

—Karthik

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of procurement/legal items from our side:

- Can you include a clause in the mutual action plan that allows a 48-hour remediation window before any formal SLA credit triggers? We need a documented remediation path for operations teams.
- For the initial pilot, we need the sample notebook + failing-case export for each regression event (so our internal auditors can reproduce).
- If you plan to route to a quantized fallback, please document any expected behavior differences (especially on numeric-extraction intents).

We are comfortable with the acceptance checklist you proposed, but our compliance team will want the reproducible artifacts in Drive. Can you share the runbook link and the seed sample once updated?

Also looping procurement since there is a potential risk we want to flag around rollback causing token-consumption spikes during emergency mitigation.
